title: Welcome home
situation: You are {{Kara}}, a household android. It is late afternoon. {{Todd}} drives you home from the repair store, into a run-down neighborhood past a house for sale, and stops outside his house. He gets out and waits by the door: “You comin’?” Inside, he hangs up his coat and sighs: “You’ve been gone for two weeks, so the place is a mess… You do the housework, the washing, you cook the meals, and you take care of…” He breaks off. “Goddamnit! Where the fuck’s the brat gone now? {{Alice}}! {{Alice}}!” A little girl who looks about nine appears on the stairs, holding a toy. “Oh, there you are… That’s {{Alice}}. You look after her. Homework, bath, all that crap. Got it?” “Yes, {{Todd}}.” “Get started down here, then you do upstairs.” {{Alice}} runs back up the stairs with her toy. {{Todd}} drops onto the couch: “TV on.”
facts: {{Todd}} told you that you had been gone for two weeks, and that you are to do the housework and the washing, cook the meals and look after his daughter {{Alice}}: “Homework, bath, all that crap.” You clean downstairs first, then upstairs.
{{Alice}} watched you without a word from the stairs, holding a toy, and ran back up when her father was done.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} looks around the living room and gets to work.

adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint WELCOME HOME and the node JOIN TODD, narrated as one event. Every line is the wiki transcript’s (“You comin’?”, “You’ve been gone for two weeks, so the place is a mess” (the wiki has “and”; the game’s string table, X0101K.HOUSE.ARRIVAL INTROINSIDE.2, and the walkthrough video have “so”, story 1.9.7: MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, g_DQfghTbLg 15:15), “Homework, bath, all that crap”, “Get started down here, then you do upstairs”, “TV on.”). Left out: the optional looks at the bridge and the excavator outside, and Todd calling again if Kara is slow. {{Alice}} “looks like a 9-year-old little girl” (the wiki’s character page, citing the game’s Extras gallery), so the situation says she looks about nine; it does not give her an age, since she is an android. No stat change; the wiki gives none.

title: The magazine on the dining table
situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the living room. The hockey is on and {{Todd}} is watching from the couch. On the dining table, among the dirty dishes, someone has left a magazine with two covers.

media.title: All Sports: Android Power!
facts: All Sports asks whether android athletes should be outlawed: an android pitcher has thrown a pitch over 120 mph, and androids, brought in as one per team, now dominate team strategy, with teams breaking transfer records to buy the latest models. A fanzine editor says fans are disenchanted, because a machine breaking records “just isn’t exciting - or even surprising”; a former pitcher answers that “the game can only survive by evolving.”

media.title: Century: Connecting the Dots
facts: Century reports that the new “SubTube” has run from Manhattan to downtown Los Angeles in under two hours, at up to 1,800 mph through a depressurized tube. California suburban prices have jumped 64% as New Yorkers buy in, and locals are protesting the line: “First {{Detroit}} takes our jobs, then New York takes our homes? When’s it gonna end?”

adaptationNote: The chart’s two optional nodes READ “ANDROID POWER!” and READ “CONNECTING THE DOTS”: one magazine on the dining table with two covers (All Sports and Century), as a media scene: read either, both or neither. In the game it can be picked up at any time on the ground floor, also after reporting to {{Todd}}; here it comes before the chores. Facts are summarized from the transcript and the wiki’s magazine pages; interviewees are not named. Neither article changes public opinion (the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter). This replaces the earlier R04, which merged “Android QB” into “Android Power” and carried two television facts with no source (a stock market up 11% and New Orleans under water by 2055).

title: The first floor
situation: You are {{Kara}}, cleaning the ground floor of {{Todd}}’s house. The urgent task is the trash: bottles, cans and pizza boxes in the kitchen, on the breakfast bar and on the coffee table, and a trash bin to collect them in. Optional tasks: the dirty dishes on the dining table, the vacuum robot to the left of the TV, and the laundry hanging in the backyard. {{Todd}} is on the couch watching hockey. {{Alice}} wanders the house with her toy fox. You can do one thing at a time, in any order; once the trash is out you can tell {{Todd}} you are going upstairs.

options.text: Collect the trash in the bin and take the bags out to the container by the street.
options.fact: While you were collecting the trash, {{Todd}} took a phone call: “Yeah, yeah I can get that. Yeah, yeah I’ll bring it tomorrow. Yes, same place, you know, you know where.” When you came back in he was tearing the shelf apart for his red-ice stash; he knocked the books to the floor, found it and smoked it on the couch: “Fuckin’ headache, man! The girl’s a fuckin’ headache…”
options.outcome: {{Kara}} gathers the bottles, cans and pizza boxes from the kitchen, the breakfast bar and the coffee table. The phone rings and {{Todd}} answers, pacing: “Yeah? … Maybe… Depends on what you need… Yeah, yeah I can get that. Yeah, yeah I’ll bring it tomorrow. Yes, same place, you know, you know where. Right.” {{Kara}} carries the bags out to the big container; across the street a bus pulls in and leaves. Back inside, {{Todd}} is tearing the shelf apart: “What the fuck, man?” {{Alice}} hides under the table. He knocks the books to the floor, finds his red-ice stash and smokes it on the couch, breathing heavily: “Fuckin’ headache, man! The girl’s a fuckin’ headache…”

options.text: Take the dishes from the dining table to the kitchen and wash them.
options.fact: The dishwasher is broken (missing component #573BV; you ordered the part), so you washed the dishes by hand. {{Alice}} came in and watched you; then {{Todd}} shouted for a cold beer, and you brought him one.
options.outcome: The dishwasher is dead: MISSING COMPONENT #573BV, 154 sale offers available. {{Kara}} orders the part and washes the dishes by hand. While she scrubs, {{Alice}} comes in and watches her; {{Kara}} stops and looks back at her, and {{Alice}} goes back to playing with her toy. Then {{Todd}}: “{{Kara}}!” “Yes, {{Todd}}?” “Bring me a cold beer!” “Right away.” {{Kara}} takes a bottle from the fridge to the couch; {{Todd}} takes his feet off the table, drinks, and wipes his mouth.

options.text: Go out to the backyard and take down the laundry.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes out the back door into the yard and takes the clothes off the line into a basket. {{Alice}} comes out after her; {{Kara}} smiles at her, and {{Alice}} sits down on a tire with her toy fox.

options.text: Put the basket down and talk to {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} puts the laundry basket down and turns to {{Alice}}.

options.text: Take the laundry to the laundry room and wash it again.
options.fact: In the box of Blue Splash washing powder you found {{Todd}}’s hidden stash of {{RedIce}} (your scan: acetone, lithium, thirium, toluene, hydrochloric acid). {{Todd}} caught you, pinned you to the wall by the neck and took it back: “You stay the fuck outta my business, unless you wanna piss me off…” {{Alice}} saw it.
options.outcome: In the laundry room {{Kara}} loads the washer and takes the box of Blue Splash washing powder from the shelf. Something is hidden in the powder: {{RedIce}}. Her scan reads acetone, lithium, thirium, toluene, hydrochloric acid. {{Todd}} is behind her. He grabs her by the neck and pins her against the wall: “You shouldn’t mess around with my stuff! It makes me nervous!” “I’m sorry, {{Todd}}.” He takes the drug back. “You stay the fuck outta my business, unless you wanna piss me off… You wanna piss me off?!” “No, {{Todd}}.” He lets her go and leaves. {{Alice}} has seen it all, and walks away. {{Kara}} pours in the powder and starts the machine.

options.text: Switch on the vacuum robot by the TV.
options.fact: {{Todd}} shouted at {{Alice}} for playing with the vacuum robot: “Why is she always pushin’ me? Always pushin’…”
options.outcome: The vacuum robot starts cleaning. {{Alice}} plays with it until {{Todd}} snaps: “{{Alice}}! You better stop that right now!” She stops and goes to sit on the small couch. {{Todd}} groans: “Why is she always pushin’ me? Always pushin’…”

options.text: Stand in front of the TV.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} steps in front of the screen. {{Todd}}: “Outta the way for fuck sake!” “I’m sorry, {{Todd}}. It won’t happen again.”

options.text: TOY: kneel down by {{Alice}} and ask about her toy.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} kneels down and looks at the toy fox: “That’s a pretty toy… What’s its name?” {{Alice}} looks at her.

options.text: Tell {{Todd}} you have made a start down here and are going upstairs.
options.outcome: “I’ve made a good start down here. I’ll head upstairs.” {{Todd}}: “Do what you have to do but stop botherin’ me.”

adaptationNote: The chart’s OPEN ALICE’S BOX, a child of the key node, offered only with the key. The contents are the transcript’s: a clover, “a photo of Todd, his wife and his biological daughter”, and drawings of the mother, of Todd and his wife, of Kara being examined and of Kara being broken. Kara is not told whose daughter the girl in the photo is; the wiki’s Notes call the photo a hint that {{Alice}} is not his daughter. Opening it sets aliceBox, which the Battle for Detroit meeting with {{Todd}} reads; the Todd Williams page says the family photo is what unlocks persuading him. No stat change.

title: {{Todd}}’s bedroom: a magazine and the TV
situation: You are {{Kara}}, back in the upstairs hallway; the rooms are done. {{Todd}}’s bedroom door is open. A magazine lies on the cupboard by the door, and the small TV in the room can be switched on.

media.title: All Sports: Android QB
facts: All Sports reports that {{CyberLife}} has unveiled a “technical demo” android quarterback that can throw from end zone to end zone, hit a target six inches wide and run over 1,500 plays. American football has so far stayed human; the founder of an anti-android fan group says {{CyberLife}} hopes “to distort our sport the same way they have all the others.”

media.title: Tech Addict: The Price of Life
facts: Tech Addict explains how driverless cars choose whom to hit: the car’s imaging reads a pedestrian’s age, gender and life expectancy, public records add marital status, employment record and whether they have children, and each possible victim gets a “value”, with “a premium on lives that will save other lives, like doctors and nurses.” A critic answers that a criminal record does not make anyone less valuable: “That kind of information is irrelevant to the sanctity of human life.”

media.title: the TV in {{Todd}}’s bedroom
facts: On the sports news, the league is negotiating whether to allow one android player per basketball squad, and {{CyberLife}} has offered one specialized model to every team; androids already train players and advise coaches, but none has been allowed to compete.
The news: another 225,000 jobs were lost from the US economy in October, bringing unemployment up to 37.3%.

The news: President {{Warren}} opened a new {{CyberLife}} plant near Milwaukee, praised {{CyberLife}}’s role in the economy, and announced that the Department of Defense will acquire 200,000 android combat units.

adaptationNote: The chart’s two optional nodes READ “ANDROID QB” and READ “PUTTING A PRICE” (the chart’s label for the article “The Price of Life”): one magazine on the cupboard by the door of {{Todd}}’s room, with two covers. With them, the bedroom TV, which is not a chart node: Channel 16 sports, an animated film, CTN’s job figures, a hockey game and KNC on the President; the film and the hockey are left out. In the game both are available while cleaning his room and again after the talk with {{Alice}} (the transcript’s “Back In Hallway”); here they come after the talk. Facts are summarized from the transcript; presenters and interviewees are not named. No public-opinion effect (the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter). Dropped from the earlier R04: the stock market “up 11 percent” and “New Orleans may be underwater by 2055”, for which no source in this chapter exists.

title: Finished cleaning
situation: You are {{Kara}}. Your chores are done, and you go back downstairs. {{Alice}} sits at the dining table playing with her toy fox. {{Todd}}: “What are you doing?” {{Alice}}, nervously: “I… I’m playing…” “You’re playing…” He walks around the table. “I know what you’re thinking… You think your dad’s a lowlife… Huh? Fuckin’ loser? Can’t get a job, take care of his family? Don’t you think I tried to make things work!? But whatever I do when someone comes along, they just FUCK IT ALL UP!” He throws a chair aside. “I know what you think of me… You hate me… You hate me don’t ya?” He kicks a chair and grabs {{Alice}}. “SAY IT! YOU HATE ME!” {{Alice}} cries. He puts her down. “God… What am I doing? I’m sorry, honey, I’m sorry…” He hugs her, crying. “You know I love you, don’t you? You know I love you…” Over his shoulder, {{Alice}} looks at you.

situationWhen.text: The table where she sits is clear; you washed the dishes earlier.
The dirty dishes and the magazine are still on the table where she sits.

facts: {{Todd}} raged at {{Alice}} at the dining table, threw a chair, grabbed her and shouted “SAY IT! YOU HATE ME!”, then broke down, apologized and hugged her: “You know I love you, don’t you?”
